statement_verbatim: statement: Colon means hierarchical descent (unlimited depth); dot means lateral variation (keep shallow).

statement: A produced or consumed artifact/contract identity must be theme-first — it must
  parse as the grammar {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?, every colon/dot
  token must be kebab-case, and the leading theme must be declared in plan/_themes.yaml.
statement: 'A contract URN exactly matches the artifact name, preserving colons and dots: contract:{artifact_name}.'
statement: Artifact names must satisfy the format, semantic, and technical validation rules.

statement: The product capability and feature names already on disk are scanned for verb-object
  conformance and the non-conforming ones are reported with a count, so naming drift
  is visible and its size is known. This reports; it never blocks.

statement: An artifact is a produced-or-consumed unit of the domain — a theme-namespaced,
  URN-identified thing (material, contract, schema) that product capabilities exchange and that DESIRED OUTCOMES
  and acceptances prove. Its identity follows the canonical naming pattern (theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant)
  and mirrors its declared location. This is a planner domain-decomposition artifact
  naming WHAT is exchanged; its runtime realization as flow variables in flight is a coder/tester
  concern. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes
  that require it.

statement: A product capability's produced artifacts carry a contract URN (contract:{...}) and a telemetry URN (telemetry:{...})
  following the artifact-naming grammar.

statement: Product capability sizing has two orthogonal axes — intrinsic footprint (how much work is inside) and coupling complexity (whether the cut is correct). Complexity is modeled as super-linear in cross-capability coupling, not additive in component count.

statement: Report each product capability's cross-capability coupling complexity (fan_in x fan_out over the produce->consume name graph); flag product capabilities above a soft, config-driven threshold. Advisory and non-blocking.

statement: A product capability is a separable, semantically-coherent unit of work within a journey
  — a single subject/action/goal that consumes and produces declared artifacts and
  composes with sibling product capabilities into user/system flows without forming a produce/consume cycle.
  This is a planner domain-decomposition artifact naming a unit of the domain; how the
  unit executes at runtime is a coder/tester concern. This node is an advisory semantic
  anchor — it enforces nothing directly; the enforceable parts of this meaning are
  decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes that require it.

statement: A product capability's features are declared as an array of URN objects (feature:{capability-slug}:{feature-name});
  the legacy object map is deprecated.
statement: A product capability's _features.yaml lists every feature module and its current status.

statement: Logical identifiers (URNs, slugs, YAML refs) use kebab-case; the filesystem (directories, manifest
  files, feature files) uses snake_case.

statement: A product capability slug must be verb-object — kebab-case, at least two tokens, the
  leading token a verb from the convention verb lexicon, and no connective tokens.
  Brand or proper-noun slugs must be listed explicitly in capability.convention.yaml
  verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions; an implicit exception is a violation.
statement: The directed product capability graph built from produce->consume artifact NAMES must be acyclic; no strongly-connected component may span more than one product capability.

statement: produce[] entries declare name + contract + telemetry (optional to/urn/version); consume[]
  entries declare name (optional from/contract/telemetry/urn/version).

statement: Refine ambiguous input into a structured product capability by extracting subject, action, goal, context,
  outcome, produce/consume artifacts, and theme.

statement: 'A product capability must be semantically coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable, produce
  is owned, consume is foreign, and at least one produce is external.'
